project.name: COLREGS Navigator
project.one_liner: A maritime collision-avoidance rules engine and visualizer: place two vessels on a nautical chart, and it classifies the encounter under the real International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea (COLREGS Rules 11-18), states which vessel must give way, and shows the exact rule and geometry behind that verdict.
project.type: Software engineering portfolio project (built for job interviews), not a commercial product
project.current_build_state: Core interactive sandbox is live: drag-to-position vessels on an SVG chart, live COLREGS classification, reasoning-trail panel with rule citations. Save/share links and a curated gallery of classic encounters are the next phase, not yet built.
project.tech_stack: Next.js 16 / React 19 / TypeScript / Tailwind CSS v4, hand-rolled SVG chart (no canvas/game-engine library), tRPC + Prisma + Postgres backend. Whatever visual system this brief produces must be realistically implementable in Tailwind CSS + plain SVG/CSS — no dependency on a component or animation library the project hasn't already chosen.

audience_and_goal.primary_audience: Technical recruiters and engineering hiring managers skimming a portfolio link, plus interviewers who will spend a few minutes actually using it
audience_and_goal.attention_budget: 3-5 seconds to decide 'this looks like serious, senior-level work' before they either dig in or bounce
success_definition: Within seconds, a visitor understands what the tool does and that it's not a toy CRUD app
The interactive demo (drag a vessel, watch the verdict update) reads as the hero moment, not a buried feature
The visual language signals precision and domain authority (navigation/maritime instrumentation), not generic 'AI-generated startup landing page'
Engineering depth is visible, not just claimed: rule citations, live reasoning trail, and clean data visualization should be front and center
audience_and_goal.explicitly_not_the_goal: This is not a consumer maritime app and not a sales page — no pricing, no signup funnel, no marketing fluff. The 'conversion' being optimized for is a recruiter thinking 'I want to talk to whoever built this.'

brand_personality.tone_analogy: Somewhere between an ECDIS/chart-plotter bridge display and a modern SaaS analytics dashboard (think Stripe or Linear-level visual polish) — nautical instrumentation aesthetic, not cartoon-nautical (no rope borders, anchors-as-clipart, or pirate/beach vibes)

visual_direction.concept: Modern chart-plotter / bridge-display aesthetic: a dark or deep-navy 'navigation display' mode for the hero/marketing surface, transitioning into the cleaner light 'chart paper' mode already built for the working sandbox tool itself.
motifs_to_explore: Subtle nautical chart graticule / grid lines as background texture (already used sparingly in the built sandbox)
Compass rose or bearing-ring as a hero graphic element, functioning almost like a logo mark
Radar-sweep or bearing-line animation as a tasteful hero-section motion accent (restrained, not distracting)
Monospace numeric readouts (bearing°, speed in knots, distance) styled like instrument-panel digits, for authenticity
Vessel icons as clean geometric wedge/hull shapes (already the built convention) rather than illustrated ship icons

two_display_modes.instrument_dark: For hero/landing/marketing surfaces aimed at first impressions — deep navy/charcoal background, high-contrast readouts, glowing accent color, feels like a bridge display at night
two_display_modes.chart_light: For the actual working sandbox tool — already implemented as a clean, minimal, off-white 'chart paper' surface (slate-50 background, white panel surfaces, teal accent) so the tool itself stays highly legible and non-fatiguing during real use

color_system.note_to_designer: Two color layers exist. The chrome/brand palette below is open for a bolder redesign. The domain-semantic overlay colors are LOCKED — they already carry real meaning in the shipped app (give-way vs. stand-on vessel, doubt/ambiguous verdicts) and must not be changed or reused for anything else, or the app's own visual logic breaks.

chrome_palette_open_to_redesign.ask: Propose a more distinctive, memorable chrome palette for the hero/marketing surface (dark instrument-panel mode) that still complements the locked domain colors below rather than competing with them. Teal is a reasonable anchor to keep or evolve, but not mandatory.

domain_semantic_colors_LOCKED_do_not_cha.mutual_obligation_hull: slate-400 #94A3B8 (deliberately not amber, to avoid clashing with the doubt signal below)

typography.current_baseline: System UI sans stack for all UI text; monospace for numeric geometric readouts (bearing, speed, distance) so digits align in tabular columns. Only two weights used: 400 and 600.
typography.ask: A hero/display typeface pairing is open for exploration for the marketing surface (e.g. a distinctive display face for headlines, paired with the existing clean sans for body/UI) as long as it's a normal web font (Google Fonts or similar, no paid/exotic license needed) and doesn't fight the instrument-panel monospace numerals.

layout_and_key_screens.purpose: First thing a recruiter sees. Must communicate the concept and domain-depth in one glance.
must_include: A strong, specific headline (not generic 'AI-powered app' copy) that states the real mechanic: place two vessels, get a COLREGS verdict with cited rule and geometry
A live or near-live preview of the actual sandbox chart (not a mockup screenshot) as the dominant visual element
A short credibility strip: e.g. 'Rules 11-18 of the actual International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea' — the real-world grounding is a selling point

layout_and_key_screens.screen: Interactive sandbox (already built, may get a visual refresh)
layout_and_key_screens.purpose: The core loop and demo centerpiece: chart panel (SVG, drag-to-position/rotate vessels), control panel (speed/vessel-type), reasoning-trail panel (verdict banner + rule citations + geometry)
layout_and_key_screens.constraint: Must stay highly legible and low-fatigue for real interactive use — this is the 'chart_light' display mode, not the dramatic dark hero mode

layout_and_key_screens.screen: Gallery of classic encounters (Phase 5, not yet built)
layout_and_key_screens.purpose: A curated set of 5-8 textbook COLREGS scenarios (clean head-on, classic crossing, overtaking) a visitor can browse and load with one click
layout_and_key_screens.must_include: Small preview thumbnails of each scenario's chart geometry, not just text list items

layout_and_key_screens.screen: Shared scenario view (Phase 5, not yet built)
layout_and_key_screens.purpose: Read/replay view when someone opens a shared link — same visual language as the sandbox, always shows a freshly computed verdict

signature_moments_to_nail: The verdict banner: large, confident, immediate ('Crossing — Vessel A gives way') — this is the single most important UI element in the whole app
The reasoning trail: an ordered list of rule-citation + geometric-fact steps that reads like a legible audit trail, not a debug log
Live drag interaction: dragging a vessel and watching the verdict, hull colors, and bearing line update with zero lag or flicker should feel satisfying and precise

motion.philosophy: Restrained and purposeful, instrument-panel smoothness rather than playful bounce. Motion should reinforce precision (smooth interpolation of bearing lines/hull rotation during drag) not decorate.
acceptable: smooth live updates during drag with no jank
a subtle radar-sweep or bearing-line animation as a hero-section idle accent
avoid: anything that delays the user seeing the live verdict

content_voice.tone: Precise, matter-of-fact, technically confident — written the way a ship's officer or a well-documented engineering spec would write, not marketing copy
content_voice.example_headline_style: 'Two vessels. One rulebook. See exactly who must give way and why.' rather than 'Revolutionize your maritime workflow!'
content_voice.example_error_copy_already_established: 'Unable to classify' / 'Vessel A and Vessel B are at the same position — drag one apart to resume live classification.'

technical_constraints.must_be_buildable_with: Tailwind CSS v4 utility classes + plain SVG + CSS, no canvas/WebGL, no heavyweight animation or 3D libraries
technical_constraints.accessibility: Color is never the sole signal for give-way/stand-on/mutual/doubt states — pair every color cue with a text badge (GW/SO/MUTUAL) or stroke-style difference (solid vs. dashed), already an established convention
technical_constraints.responsiveness: Should degrade gracefully to a usable single-column layout on tablet/mobile for a recruiter briefly checking on a phone, even though the primary use case is desktop

inspiration_references: ECDIS / marine chart-plotter bridge displays (instrument authenticity)
Aviation glass-cockpit UI (precision readouts, restrained color use)
Modern developer-tool SaaS polish (Stripe, Linear, Vercel) for the chrome/typography/spacing quality bar
Real nautical chart cartography (graticule lines, chart symbol conventions) for texture, used sparingly as an accent not as decoration
deliverables_requested: A hero/landing page visual direction (dark instrument-panel mode) with headline treatment and a way to showcase the live sandbox as the centerpiece
A refreshed or validated chrome color palette + type pairing, respecting the locked domain-semantic colors
Component styling direction for: verdict banner, reasoning-trail entries, vessel role badges (GW/SO/MUTUAL), gallery scenario cards
Any reusable motif (compass rose, bearing-ring mark) that could double as a lightweight logo/favicon for the project
non_negotiables: Never change the meaning-bearing colors (red=give-way, green=stand-on, slate=mutual, amber=doubt) or reuse them for non-domain UI chrome
Never obscure or shrink the reasoning trail / rule citations in favor of pure decoration — explainability is this project's entire thesis
No stock ship photography, no cartoon/pirate maritime theming, no generic AI-startup gradient-blob aesthetic
